svg.title: Grok Bot: which lines actually isolate
svg.desc: Users are isolated by a Firecracker microVM. Bots of one user share a computer; a Bot and a screen are not security boundaries. Auto Review and local execution are action controls.
svg.text: Which lines actually isolate
Between users: isolated
One Firecracker microVM per Cursor user
Its own kernel, memory, and virtual devices
One user cannot reach another user's computer
Hardware-level isolation, not something a Bot name provides
Between one user's Bots: not isolated
Shared files, browser logins, and CLI credentials
Separate screens, still one computer
Hiding a Bot does not pause routines or create a boundary
Deleting a Bot does not clear shared files or sign-ins
A separate computer and credentials means another Cursor user
Action control is another layer, not isolation
Auto Review: shell, plugins, computer use, automation writes
Also Cloud Agent and subagent delegation
Not every side effect, such as memory writes or most settings
Local execution is separate from cloud Auto Review
OAuth tokens stay on the connector backend
Blocking a plugin does not block that website
Learning schematic. A Bot is not a security boundary.
Per-Bot strong isolation, the computer-use stack, and a public API to call one Bot are undocumented.
Sources: public Teams, Security, and Approvals docs · 2026-09-28
